About Me

A practice built on breath, not performance

I've spent years studying and teaching yoga as something closer to a conversation with yourself than a workout. My classes move slowly, with long holds and unhurried transitions, so that the body has time to actually listen.

I call my approach theagamyoga — agam being the Tamil word for the inner self, the interior world we rarely make time to visit. Every session I teach is built around one question: what does this body need today, not what does it need to prove?

My students describe my classes as equal parts grounding and gentle challenge — accessible if you're a complete beginner, and quietly deep if you've practiced for years.

— Anitha

My Style

Three ideas behind every class I teach

மௌனம்
Mounam — Stillness

I open and close every class in real silence. Not a formality — I give you a few full minutes to arrive in the body before any movement begins.

மூச்சு
Moochu — Breath

I let breath lead every movement, never the other way round. If your breath gets short, I'll tell you the pose is too big — that's the only rule I hold to.

மெய்ப்பொருள்
Meiporul — Essence

My alignment cues are about what's true for your body that day, not a textbook shape. I offer modifications freely — you'll never need to apologize for taking them.
